question: Graphical User Interface (GUI) was developed during which of the following generations of computer?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fourth Generation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The GUI was first developed at Xerox PARC by Alan Kay, Douglas Engelbart, and a group of other researchers in 1981. Later, Apple introduced the Lisa computer with a GUI on January 19, 1983.
 
• Graphical User Interface (GUI) was developed during the **Fourth Generation of computers**.
 
• These graphical elements are sometimes enhanced with sounds or visual effects like transparency and drop shadows. Using these objects, a user can use the computer without having to know commands.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A GUI (graphical user interface) is a system of interactive visual components for computer software.
 
• A GUI displays objects that convey information, and represent actions that can be taken by the user.
 
• A GUI includes GUI objects like icons, cursors, and buttons. 
 
• The Icons are used to represent a specific operation. A settings bottom is represented by a gear icon.
 
• Menus contain the set of operations that can be performed on the following window. Menus mainly use drop-down drawers which contain multiple buttons.
 
• The graphs are also used to represent the data related to the system. Like the temperature of the motherboard is represented by the graphs.
 
• The command lines are not part of the graphical interface, but they work in the background.
